title: Chapter close — $q$-Geometric Langlands Correspondence
html:
The q-geometric Langlands correspondence assembled here yields a single functorial statement: the substrate parameter q controls both the categorical structure of \mathbf{C} and the spectral distribution of its associated L-functions. This closes the main argument of the paper, packaging the substrate arithmetic — Tannaka–Krein duality on the Hopf side, the Weil-bound stability on the spectral side, and the geometric Riemann hypothesis exposition that ties them together — into that one correspondence.

The appendices that follow record the supporting material that would have over-burdened the main narrative. The knot-periodic table catalogues the categorical assignment of knots to chemical elements; the transfer-matrix appendix records the canonical \sigma-word presentations used in the Hecke reductions; the atomic-mass appendix lists the per-isotope categorical predictions against CODATA; the Q-value and surreal-bound appendices fill in the technical layers that the main text gestures at. Readers who want the substrate-arithmetic in one piece should re-read the braids-and-knots and observation chapters with this Langlands synthesis in mind.
